extracted.intended_audience: Graduate students applying to the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and submitting NSF GRFP applications (deadlines, required materials, resources, and troubleshooting) for graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in STEM. Emphasis on 2025-specific changes (transcript policy) and where to find authoritative resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF GRFP purpose and target applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) is to help ensure the quality, vitality, and strength of the scientific and engineering workforce of the United States. The program recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students who are pursuing full-time research-based master’s and doctoral degrees in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields, including STEM education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM, including STEM education. NSF encourages applications from the full spectrum of talent that the U.S. has to offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All reference letters due by 5:00pm Eastern Time on November 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recommenders submit by this firm deadline; missing references by this time could jeopardize your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Program deadlines vary by field: November 10: Life Sciences; November 12: Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences; STEM Education and Learning; November 13: Engineering; November 14: Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit your application according to the deadline for your specific disciplinary field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NSF's 'Information for Applicants' and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF’s 'Information for Applicants' website (which includes detailed templates for each response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the official templates and instructions on the NSF site when preparing each application response.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF 2025 Application Overview Webinar
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF’s 2025 Application Overview Webinar (recorded in early October 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the recorded webinar for an overview of application components and any 2025-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive FAQ resource (nsfgrfp.org)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently Asked Questions from www.nsfgrfp.org. This is the only FAQ resource that has been updated by staff at the NSF in recent months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the nsfgrfp.org FAQ as the authoritative FAQ for prospective applicants; rely on it rather than older/outdated pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on research.gov FAQ (outdated)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONSF discourages students from relying on the FAQ page at research.gov. It was last updated in Sept. 2023, and several of the responses appear to be out-of-date, including questions about transcripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nsfgrfp.org and NSF official materials instead of the research.gov FAQ for current policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2025 transcript requirement: official transcripts only
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2025, the NSF is requiring students to upload official transcripts only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided instructions on how to request and prepare an official transcript for upload; this is a 2025-specific policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parchment transcripts: remove permission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcript you receive from the Parchment service will be permission-restricted. You’ll need to reprint it (or save another copy) and remove all permission restrictions before uploading your transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you upload a permission-restricted file it will not upload successfully. Reprint or save a new copy without permission restrictions prior to upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red 'Copy of Transcript' watermark workaround
rubrics_metrics.description: When you print a copy of an official transcript, it generates a red 'Copy of Transcript' watermark on your transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships advisors assume the watermark will not be a problem. If it bothers you, open the file, print it to PDF, save the new file with no security restrictions, and use a PDF editor to delete the watermark.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF email availability during government shutdown
rubrics_metrics.description: The grfp@nsf.gov mailbox is not being monitored during the government shutdown, so there is no one at NSF to answer questions specific to your application, your eligibility, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed alternative resources (nsfgrfp.org FAQ, recorded webinar, institutional ONSF contacts) for answers while the mailbox is unmonitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned Without Review: reporting and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If your fall 2025 application was returned without review and you’d like to share your experience with staff in ONSF or The Graduate School, please contact Dr. Vin Moscardelli at vin.moscardelli@uconn.edu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to reporting (Eos article) and community discussion (r/GRFPApps) about an uptick in applications being returned without review; contact institutional staff if affected.
